graphPatterns.modes.stale: The text differs from the pattern. Below is the last drawn state; the text is what runs.
graphPatterns.modes.textOnly: The text is what runs. “Open as pattern” draws it, when the whole query can be drawn.
graphPatterns.modes.switched: From now on the text counts. The pattern stays until you change the text. After the first change, “Open as pattern” leads back when the query can be drawn.
graphPatterns.back.canDoCypher: Cypher: MATCH with nodes and edges in one or more chains, labels and types (also A|B), direction, lengths *a..b; OPTIONAL MATCH at a node of the required pattern; WHERE with comparisons, IN, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, CONTAINS, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, joined by AND, per element also OR; parameters; RETURN of the elements or paths of the pattern; LIMIT.
graphPatterns.back.canDoGsql: GSQL: an interpreted query with exactly one SELECT block in the pattern syntax: FROM with a chain of node and edge types, direction, repetition *a..b; WHERE as above; typed parameters; LIMIT; PRINT of the matches.
graphPatterns.back.cannot: Not drawable: WITH, aggregates, ORDER BY, SKIP, UNWIND, UNION, CALL and subqueries, functions in WHERE, OR across elements, NOT on patterns, shortestPath, lengths without an upper bound, several SELECT blocks and own accumulators.
graphPatterns.empty.title: Draw what you are looking for
graphPatterns.empty.text: Start with a node and draw edges to more. Kalzit writes the query for it.
graphPatterns.empty.labelsHint: Labels from the schema of the source, with their counts.
graphPatterns.drawing.label: Pattern
graphPatterns.drawing.hint: Double-click the free area: new node. Drag from one node to another: new edge. The list shows the same pattern for the keyboard.
graphPatterns.panel.typeHint: From the schema of the source. Several labels mean “one of”.
graphPatterns.panel.typeHintGsql: From the schema of the graph. In GSQL a node has exactly one type.
graphPatterns.panel.typeEdgeHint: From {from} to {to}. A type the schema does not have between these labels finds nothing.
graphPatterns.panel.notBetween: Not between these labels in the schema
graphPatterns.panel.lengthHint: An upper bound is required; the server sets the highest. Without one a database may search the whole graph.
graphPatterns.panel.hopsInvalid: Enter whole numbers from 1, the second at least the first.
graphPatterns.panel.optionalHint: Matches come without an optional part too; where it exists, it comes along. Drawn dashed.
graphPatterns.panel.gsqlOptional: Optional parts are not possible in GSQL. A pattern query in GSQL finds complete matches only. Make the part required, or the query does not run.
graphPatterns.panel.pathNoConditions: This edge stands for a path of several edges; conditions apply to a single edge only.
graphPatterns.panel.conditionsHint: Property, comparison, value. Between elements “and” always holds; deeper logic goes in the text.
graphPatterns.panel.name: Name in the pattern
graphPatterns.panel.nameHint: The element is called this in the query.
graphPatterns.panel.nameInvalid: Letters, digits and _, starting with a letter; not a keyword.
graphPatterns.panel.chooseHint: Choose a node or an edge to edit it.
graphPatterns.condition.hint: A fixed value, or a variable: type $ and a name.
graphPatterns.condition.notNumber: {property} is a number. “{value}” is not a number.
graphPatterns.condition.badName: After $ comes a name: letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
graphPatterns.condition.empty: Enter a value, or choose “present” or “missing”.
graphPatterns.list.label: Pattern as a list
graphPatterns.warning.open: This pattern matches anything in the database: no type, no condition. Kalzit still asks for the limit only; give a node a type so the search says something.
graphPatterns.warning.edgeNotInSchema: In the schema there is no edge {type} between {from} and {to}. The pattern finds nothing this way.
graphPatterns.limit.hint: 500 unless changed, never more than the data source allows. A match is one filling of the whole pattern.
graphPatterns.count.done: {count} matches in all, counted with a second query.
graphPatterns.count.failed: The matches could not be counted.
graphPatterns.query.title: Generated query
graphPatterns.query.gsqlOptional: No query yet. The pattern has an optional part that GSQL cannot say. Choose at the element how to go on; until then nothing runs.
graphPatterns.query.hint: The server writes this text, and it is what runs. Values go to the database as parameters, never as text in the query.
graphPatterns.parameters.title: Variables of the pattern
graphPatterns.parameters.fromDashboard: Dashboard variable of the same name
graphPatterns.parameters.missing: ${name} has no value. Enter a sample value; without one the query does not run.
graphPatterns.parameters.hint: A value becomes a variable when you type $ in the value field. In Explore the sample value counts, on a dashboard the variable of the same name, in a search template what the person enters.
graphPatterns.parameters.hintDashboard: On the dashboard each variable takes the dashboard variable of the same name; its type is checked.
graphPatterns.paste.title: Paste values for ${name}
graphPatterns.paste.label: Values
graphPatterns.paste.hint: Paste a column from a table, a list or a CSV line. Each line and each separator gives one value.
graphPatterns.paste.read: {count} values found. {duplicates} repeats left out, {empty} empty lines skipped.
graphPatterns.paste.wrong: {count} values do not fit the type: {values}. Remove them or set the type to text.
graphPatterns.paste.tooMany: The list has more values than this server takes per list: at most {max}. Split the list or search by a property that describes the group.
graphPatterns.paste.withoutWrong: Take without the {count} that do not fit
graphPatterns.paste.never: The list lives in the variable, never in the query text. After the run the result says how many of the values the source has.
graphPatterns.keys: Keys in the list: N new node, E new edge from the chosen node, R turn the edge around, O optional or required, B condition, Delete remove, L drawing or list.
graphPatterns.schema.drawing: Schema of the source as a graph: {labels}
graphPatterns.schema.failed: The schema could not be loaded. Queries keep running; the builder and completion know keywords only.
graphPatterns.schema.empty: This database has no nodes yet. Once there is data, its labels show here.
graphPatterns.schema.sample: This schema comes from a sample. Rare labels and properties may be missing, types are derived. With schema info Memgraph gives the full schema; an admin of the database turns it on.
graphPatterns.schema.truncated: The database has more labels and types than Kalzit lists; the smallest are left out.
graphPatterns.schema.many: {shown} of {count} labels drawn: those with the most nodes. The list and the search know all of them; a search hit joins the drawing.
graphPatterns.schema.source.procedures: Schema from {engine}: {labels} labels, {types} edge types. Counts from the statistics of the database, as of {time}.
graphPatterns.schema.source.schemaInfo: Schema from {engine}: {labels} labels, {types} edge types. Counts from the schema info, as of {time}.
graphPatterns.schema.source.sample: From a sample of {size} nodes and edges: {labels} labels, {types} edge types. Counts within the sample, as of {time}.
graphPatterns.schema.source.catalog: Schema from {engine}: {labels} labels, {types} edge types. Counts on request (“Count” per label), as of {time}.
graphPatterns.plan.intro: The plan shows how the database works through the query: “Plan only” does not run it, “With measurement” does.
graphPatterns.plan.loading: Asking the database for the plan…
graphPatterns.plan.explained: Planned, not run. The plan shows the estimates of the database. Rows and database hits come with measurement only.
graphPatterns.plan.caption: Steps of the plan
graphPatterns.plan.unknown: Kalzit has no sentence for this operator. The name comes from the database.
graphPatterns.plan.hint.index: A filter checks every node a label scan read. With an index on that property the database would find the right ones directly. With few nodes this does not matter; with many it does. Kalzit creates no indexes; an admin of the database does.
graphPatterns.plan.hint.cartesian: Two parts without a link: every match of one is combined with every match of the other. Draw an edge between them.
graphPatterns.plan.hint.many: A step in the middle makes very many rows, of which few remain at the end. A type or a condition earlier in the pattern often helps.
graphPatterns.plan.footer: Plan from {engine}. Read from the bottom up: the database starts at the bottom, the result comes out on top. {steps} steps.
graphPatterns.plan.memgraph: Memgraph sends the plan as rows; Kalzit builds the same tree from it. Instead of database hits Memgraph gives the share of the time; it has no estimates.
graphPatterns.plan.gsqlTitle: There is no query plan for GSQL
graphPatterns.plan.gsqlText: TigerGraph gives no generally available plan for GSQL. Run time and size of the answer are under “Inspect”.
graphPatterns.plan.confirmText: “With measurement” runs the query. It runs like any query: read-only, with time limit and limit, and it counts toward your queries. For an expensive query look at “Plan only” first.
graphPatterns.plan.step.produce.title: Return the result
graphPatterns.plan.step.produce.text: Gives the rows of the result back: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.limit.title: Limit
graphPatterns.plan.step.limit.text: Stops once the limit is reached: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.expand.title: Follow edges
graphPatterns.plan.step.expand.text: Goes from each node along its edges to the next: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.expandPath.title: Follow paths
graphPatterns.plan.step.expandPath.text: Goes along paths of several edges: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.filter.title: Filter
graphPatterns.plan.step.filter.text: Keeps only what fulfils the condition: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.labelScan.title: Read all nodes of a label
graphPatterns.plan.step.labelScan.text: Goes through every node with this label and passes each on: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.allNodes.title: Read all nodes
graphPatterns.plan.step.allNodes.text: Goes through every node of the database: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.indexSeek.title: Find through an index
graphPatterns.plan.step.indexSeek.text: Finds the matching nodes directly through an index: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.projection.title: Form the columns
graphPatterns.plan.step.projection.text: Puts together the columns of the result: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.sort.title: Sort
graphPatterns.plan.step.aggregate.title: Summarize
graphPatterns.plan.step.aggregate.text: Groups rows and computes over them: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.distinct.title: Leave out repeats
graphPatterns.plan.step.skip.title: Skip
graphPatterns.plan.step.cartesian.title: Every one with every one
graphPatterns.plan.step.cartesian.text: Combines each row of one part with each row of the other: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.apply.title: Run nested
graphPatterns.plan.step.apply.text: Runs the lower part once per row of the upper: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.optional.title: Optional part
graphPatterns.plan.step.optional.text: Keeps a row also where the optional part finds nothing: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.start.title: Start
graphPatterns.plan.step.join.title: Join
graphPatterns.plan.step.join.text: Joins two parts by their shared nodes: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.edgeScan.title: Read all edges of a type
graphPatterns.plan.step.edgeScan.text: Goes through every edge of this type: {details}.
graphPatterns.plan.step.empty.title: Empty result
graphPatterns.template.label: Label
graphPatterns.template.who: Who may run it: everyone who may read this place, viewers too. They run exactly this saved query and change only the inputs. Only those who may query its data source may change it.
graphPatterns.template.what: A search template is a saved query with named inputs. A choice from values is a fixed query of the template too: the distinct values of one property, at most 200, with a search.
graphPatterns.template.first: Enter the inputs and run the search. Then the result shows here.
graphPatterns.template.listHint: {count} values. One per line, or separated by commas, semicolons or tabs.
graphPatterns.template.more: More values match than are listed; type to narrow them.
graphPatterns.template.choicesFailed: The values to choose from could not be loaded. You can still type a value.
graphPatterns.about.title: About this search
graphPatterns.about.queryHint: To read. Those who may query the data source can change it.
